---
title: "For Instructors"
---

*EDR|AI is a self-contained manual: a student working alone needs nothing
beyond the chapters and their companion Colab notebooks. This appendix is for
the other reader — the instructor who wants to teach with the book. It
presents the companion course the book grew out of and makes all of its
materials freely available.*

## Two artifacts, one loop

The book and the course are different artifacts, and keeping them distinct is
what lets each travel on its own.

- **The book** is the manual. Every chapter ends with an **It is your turn**
  section, and every chapter has its **own companion Colab notebook** (the
  badge at the top of the chapter) where a reader runs the chapter's code and
  completes that section. Worked in order, the 37 sections chain into a
  complete research project; the book stands on its own as a self-study
  path.
- **The course** wraps around the book. Its weekly **lab notebooks** are
  classroom artifacts derived from the book's chapters and shaped for live,
  50-minute flipped sessions; its **readings** are the book's chapters
  (required) with matching RDSS chapters recommended; and its **milestones**
  collect the chapters' It is your turn sections, so each graded step of the
  student's semester project is a piece of the book's chain.

When the book changes, the course material is resynchronized from it: the
English edition of the book is the source of truth for everything downstream.

## The companion course

The reference implementation is **HONR 46400 — Evidence-Driven Research**, a
semester-long Honors seminar at Purdue University (three 50-minute meetings a
week, individual research projects, a public poster conference, and an oral
evidence defense). What students learn is the working structure of
contemporary scientific research: turning curiosity into an answerable
question, designing a study whose claims are honest by construction,
producing and verifying evidence along the main pathways, stating
uncertainty like a professional, and defending a claim in public, with AI
agents doing the legwork inside that structure. Everything student-facing is
open:

- **Course website:**
  [davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/){target="_blank"}
  (syllabus, schedule, material)
- **Repository:**
  [github.com/davi-moreira/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464](https://github.com/davi-moreira/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464){target="_blank"}
- **Course datasets, one bundle:**
  [honr46400_datasets.zip](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/notebooks/data/honr46400_datasets.zip)

The weekly rhythm: Monday and Wednesday lectures are led by a student — the
day's **Student Research Lead**, whose system (handbook, preparation template,
rubric, question bank) lives with the course materials in
[`project/srl/`](https://github.com/davi-moreira/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/tree/main/project/srl){target="_blank"} —
as Socratic investigations built on the
week's lab notebook; the AI does the legwork live, and every claim it produces
is verified before it survives. Friday is a **studio**: a short retrieval quiz,
a research stand-up, and a long sprint on the week's **milestone**, worked
with the student's AI assistant (reviewer roles from an AI bench — at Purdue,
GenAI Studio — are encouraged) and submitted the same day.

## Milestones: grading the book's chain

Two things share the word "milestone", and they are different instruments.
The **book's Milestone chapters** (1–12) close each studio: the reader
concludes one by producing the studio's versioned artifact, and the book's
own rubric sits on that chapter. The **course milestones** below (M0–M15)
are the weekly graded deliverables of the companion course. They are
aligned but not identical; when this page says "milestone" unqualified, it
means the course's.

The project runs through sixteen milestones, **M0–M15**, one per week, from a
first curiosity map to a defended final research chapter. Each milestone brief
names its **book anchor**: the chapters whose It is your turn sections the
student completes and submits that week. Grading the milestone is therefore
grading a stretch of the book's chain, worked on the student's own project.
The briefs are open in the repository:
[`_research_project/2026Fall/`](https://github.com/davi-moreira/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/tree/main/_research_project/2026Fall){target="_blank"}.

## The course lab notebooks

One lab per week, nb01–nb16, each derived from the chapters it teaches. These
are the classroom counterparts of the book's companion notebooks — richer
simulations, SRL lead briefs, and session structure — and any of them opens in
free Colab.

Every lab is linked, with what it does, in the lesson-to-lab adoption
table below — that table is generated from the course crosswalk, so it
cannot drift from the book's structure the way a hand-kept list can.

## Adopting or adapting

The book is deliberately institution-agnostic, and the course material above
is open: take the whole architecture, one lab, or nothing but the reading
sequence. Instructor-side material — solution notebooks and per-meeting
session guides — lives in a private repository linked from the Instructor tab
of the course website; write to the author for access
([About the Author](author.qmd)). If you teach with EDR|AI, the author would
genuinely like to hear how it went.
